FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. Mineral fibre marine board is used for thermal insulation on board ships. Its properties widely in the process of manufacture to meet both general and specific demands. can be varied

This standard covers mineral fibre marine boards for thermal insulation intended for use on flat surfaces operating at temperatures from -50�C to 700�C. While preparing this standard considerable assistance has been derived from Naval Specification No. NCD 1413 Specification for insulation materials- Mineral Fibre Marine BoardAssistance has also been derived from BS 2972 : 1989 `Methods of tests for inorganic thermal insulating materials for formulating water absorption test'. The Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex E.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the-same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard

SHIPBUILDING - MINERAL FIBRE MARINE BOARD FOR THERMAL INSULATION - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE IS No.

Title Surface spread of flame for thermal insulation materials -Methods of test

This standard covers the requirements, and methods of sampling and test for mineral fibre marine board for thermal insulation on board ships.
2 REFERENCES

13286 : 1992

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of the terms, symbols and units given in IS 3069 : 1994 shall apply. 4 MATERIALS 4.1 The materials shall consist of rock slag, glass processed from a molten state into fibrous foam and bonded with a suitable binder. 4.2 The cloth facing shall be low alkali glass cloth, treated with a coaling compound capable to give surface finish for painting when processed and meeting the requirements and tests laid down in this standard. 4.3 The cloth in the loomstate condition shall conform to the requirements given below and the weave shall be 4 shaft satin or any other weave of equal weight and strength. The minimum breaking strength shall be determined in accordance with IS 235 : 1989 and shall comply with the following requirements:

`)The load necessary to compress the finished board to 60 percent of its initial thickness shall not be less than 20 kN/m2 and-the material shall return to 90 percent of the original thickness within five minutes of the release. 2)Any shot present in the bonded material shall not be greater than 5 mm in any dimension.

6.2 Sizes and Dimensions Boards may be supplied in thickness of 19 mm, 25 mm, 50 mm and 75 mm in sizes as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.3 Weight The weight of the finished boards, including the facing cloth shall not exceed the values given below: Thickness Weight mm kg/m2 25 2.20 50 3.70 75 5.20 6.4 Ability to Bend The mineral fibre is to be removed from a suitable sample of the finished board and the resultant facing cloth is to be folded through 90 degrees over a sharp edge without cracking. 6.5 Tolerance The dimensions of the product supplied shall not deviate from those specified by more than the tolerances given in Table 2. 7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH

7.2 Finish The surface of the board shall be capable of being painted with oil bound paints without causing the paint to crack, blister or disorder. 8 TESTS 8.1 Type Tests The type tests shall be carried out on the material to check the conformity with the requirements of the specification as given in Table 1. Fresh type tests shall be carried out whenever there is any change in the formulation of the material. 8.2 Production Test

7.1 General The surface of the finished boards shall be smooth and free-from any irregularities and defects. 2 All the tests specified in Table 1 (except thermal conductivity, and water absorption) shall constitute production tests.

IS 14335: 1996 9 PACKING AND MARKING

9.2.1 BIS Certification

Marking

9.1 Packing The material shall be packed in cartons as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 9.2 Marking The packages shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the following information: Name of the manufacturer and his recognized trade-mark, if any; b) Length, width and thickness of the material; C> Quantity; and d) Batch or lot number.

The marine board may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 9.2.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Wuenu of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The-details of conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 10 SAMPLING The method of drawing representative samples of the material and criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Annex D.

a>

ANNEX A (Table 1)
METHOD OF DETERMINATION A-l APPARATUS The apparatus comprises an arm pivoted at one end so that it may move in a vertical plane. A 6 mm diameter steel pin which has been turned to a point of 1.5 mm radius is mounted vertically on the arm 430 mm from the pivot. The weight of the arm is 350 g and an additional weight of 1.0 kg is fixed to the arm 380 mm from the pivot. The whole is fitted on to a rigid base board so that when the arm is OF PUNCTURE RESISTANCE FOR FACING CLOTH horizontal, the point is approximately 25 mm above the board. A_2 TEST PROCEDURE A sample of 250 mm x 2.50 mm fibre board with facing cloth uppermost is securely held below the point which is allowed to fall through a measured distance on to the cloth. The maximum height of fall which does not puncture the cloth is recorded.

ANNEX B (Table 1)
METHOD OF DETERMINATION B-l APPARATUS B-l.1 Asuitable testing machine to pull thesample apart with adjustable linear speed. B-2 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE B-2.1 A 100 mm x 150 mm rectangular sample is cut from the board under test and aluminium plates OF INTERLAMINAR ADHESION of the same dimensions are fixed on either side of the sample using a contact adhesive. B-3 TEST PROCEDURE B-3.1 The plates are then placed in a suitable testing machine and pulled apart at 20 mm/min. The maximum load is recorded and from it the interlaminar adhesion in kN/m" is calculated.

3

IS 14335 : 1996

ANNEX C (Table 1)
WATER ABSORPTION C-l GENERAL TEST

This method specifies testing of mineral fibre marine board for thermal insulation under conditions of partial immersion in water. C-2 SPECIMENS
C-2.1 Number and Size

150 mm x 150 mm preferably 25 mm internally, fitted with a lid of the same material. C-3 PROCEDURE C-3.1 Partial Immersion Suspend the specimen, prepared as in C-2.2, vertically with one 150 mm x 25 mm side immersed 6 mm below the surface of tap water for 48 h. Maintain the water at constant level by means of a slow constant feed and fixed overflow pipe. At the end of the period of immersion, suspend the specimen by one corner and allow to drain for 5 minutes. When applicable, wipe off the excess surface water with a dry cloth or remove by the careful application of blotting paper. Weigh the specimen immediately. C-4 EXPRESSION OF RESULTS The results of the tests shall be expressed as follows: a) The increase in mass expressed in kg of water per m2 of immersed horizontal surface. b) The bulk density of the specimen before testing. c) The condition of the specimen, particularly any signs of deterioration,

Six to nine specimens shall be taken for this test. The size of the specimen shall be 150 mm2 and preferably not less than 25 mm thick. C-2.2 Preparation
C-2.2.1 of Test Specimens

Weigh the specimens as received and subsequently dry to constant mass. Determine the dry mass of the specimen. For materials having a recommended upper temperature limit of less than 12O"C,dry the specimen in a dessicator. Where the upper temperature limit is 120�C or over, dry the specimen in a ventilated oven at 105�C to 110�C. C-2.2.2 Loose, fibrous, granular and powdered materials shall be carefully and evenly packed to a specified bulk density into an open topped, perforated sheet metal or gauze container, measuring
